issues.title: Item-frame culling state causes 3D backpack models to disappear based on camera direction
issues.body:
## Description

With More Culling enabled, 3D backpack models from both Sophisticated Backpacks and Traveler’s Backpack partially or completely disappear when the camera faces certain world directions.

The affected direction covers roughly a 100-degree arc around north. Turning away from that direction—or sometimes looking downward—makes the models reappear.

Disabling More Culling’s item-frame rendering and culling options resolves the problem:

```json
{
  "useCustomItemFrameRenderer": false,
  "itemFrameMapCulling": false,
  "useItemFrameLOD": false,
  "useItemFrame3FaceCulling": false
}
```

Removing More Culling also resolves it.

## Observed behavior

The issue affects multiple 3D rendering contexts:

- Sophisticated Backpack icons completely disappear from the hotbar.
- Traveler’s Backpack icons partially disappear from the hotbar.
- A backpack held in the player’s hand disappears.
- A backpack worn on the player’s back disappears.
- Backpack models disappear from the player paper doll in the Accessories screen.
- Using Freecam confirms that visibility is controlled by the active camera’s world-facing direction.

The normal inventory screen is not affected. Backpack icons remain fully visible in regular inventory slots, even while the hotbar, held model, worn model, or Accessories paper doll is affected.

All backpack tiers and variants behave similarly, including:

- Every Sophisticated Backpack tier
- Dyed Sophisticated Backpacks
- Every Traveler’s Backpack tier
- Special Traveler’s Backpack variants such as Squid and Magma

This occurs with two independently developed backpack mods, so it does not appear to be specific to one backpack model.

## Expected behavior

3D item models should remain visible in the hotbar, hand, worn-equipment render, and player preview regardless of the camera’s world-facing direction.

Item-frame culling optimizations should not affect later item rendering outside item frames.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Minecraft 1.21.1 with NeoForge, More Culling, and either Sophisticated Backpacks or Traveler’s Backpack.
2. Put a backpack in the hotbar.
3. Optionally equip another backpack on the player’s back or hold one in hand.
4. Slowly rotate the camera through all compass directions.
5. Near north, observe the backpack model partially or completely disappear.
6. Turn away from that direction and observe it reappear.
7. Open
```

issues.title: Cull-shape fallback uses getOcclusionShape without re-checking canOcclude, culling neighbours of noOcclusion() blocks
issues.body:
**Environment**

| | |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 26.1.2, Fabric |
| MoreCulling | `moreculling-fabric-26.1.2-1.7.2.jar` |
| Config | `useBlockStateCulling = true`, `useOnModdedBlocksByDefault = true` (defaults) |
| Also loaded | Sodium 0.9.1, Cloth Config 26.1.154; Fabric Loader 0.19.3, Fabric API 0.154.2+26.1.2, Java 25 |
| OS / GPU | macOS 15, Apple M2 Max (mechanism is platform-independent) |
| Affected content | any mod block registered `noOcclusion()` whose class has no `getShape` override — reproduced with our Create addon ports on Create Fly `26.1.2-6.0.9-4` |

## Summary

When a model declares neither `cullshapes` nor `useModelShape`, the block-state cull-shape
initialisation falls back to `getBlock().getOcclusionShape(state)` — but that fallback is taken
*after* the `canOcclude` branch and does not re-check `canOcclude`. For a `noOcclusion()` block whose
class does not override `getShape`, `BlockBehaviour#getOcclusionShape` returns the default full cube,
`Block.isShapeFullBlock` passes, and MoreCulling installs `FULL_BLOCK_OCCLUSION_SHAPES` — so every
neighbouring face touching that block is culled. In-world this reads as an x-ray hole: the top face of
the floor under a machine disappears.

## Steps to reproduce / Evidence

1. Any block registered with `noOcclusion()` (so vanilla never fills `occlusionShapesByFace`) whose
   class has **no `getShape` override**, and whose model is not a full cube. Our repro used
   `createaddition:alternator` and `createaddition:electric_motor` (Create Fly 26.1.2).
2. Place it on a solid floor — we used a solid 8-deep white-concrete slab so a culled top face shows
   the fully-culled dark interior rather than a lit cavity — and look at the contact edge at a
   grazing ~20° angle.
3. Bare dev client: floor intact. Add `moreculling 1.7.2` (+ cloth-config, sodium): floor gone.

Pixel counts (green terrain visible through the white slab, one screenshot per facing, flywheel
render path; the BER path is identical, i.e. this is chunk-mesh culling, not block-entity rendering):

| shot | dev client | + MoreCulling | + MoreCulling, block fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alt_north` | 0 | 1150 | 0 |
| `alt_south` | 0 | 1670 | 0 |
| `alt_east` | 1 | 1830 | 0 |
| `alt_west` | 33 | 2403 | 21 |
| `alt_up` | 48 | 1480 | 67 |
| `alt_down` | 75 | 543 | 113 |

(Residuals are a distant tree line that Sodium draws further than the vanilla dev client; the paired
crops are unambiguous.) Screenshots available on request (before / reproduced / fixed, per facing).

We also read the decision value back directly by reflecting into
`ca.fxco.moreculling.api.blockstate.StateCullingShapeCache#moreculling$getFaceCullingShape(Direction.DOWN)`:
affected blocks report **FULL BLOCK**; after the block declares an empty occlusion shape they report
**EMPTY**, matching `minecraft:white_concrete` = FULL BLOCK as a positive control.

## Root cause

`ca.fxco.moreculling.mixin.models.cullshape.BlockStateBase_cullShapeMixin#moreculling$initCustomCullingShape`
(method confirmed present by `javap` on the 1.7.2 jar; the class also carries the shadowed
`canOcclude` / `occlusionShapesByFace` fields). Models opt into a real cull shape via
`Deserializer_cullShapeMixin`; ours declare neither key, so `moreculling$getCullingShape` returns
`null` and the fallback runs:

```java
if (shape == null) {
    if (canOcclude) { cullingShapesByFace = occlusionShapesByFace; return; }  // vanilla path
    shape = getBlock().getOcclusionShape(asState());   // <-- canOcclude is NOT re-checked here
}
if (Block.isShapeFullBlock(shape)) cullingShapesByFace = FULL_BLOCK_OCCLUSION_SHAPES;  // culls all 6
```

`BlockBehaviour#getOcclusionShape(BlockState)` defaults to `state.getShape(...)`, and `Block`'s
default shape is a full cube — so for `canOcclude == false` blocks without a `getShape` override the
fallback manufactures a full-block cull shape out of nothing. Vanilla never reaches this value:
`BlockStateBase.initCache` only populates `occlusionShapesByFace` when `canOcclude` (verified by
`javap` on the 26.1.2 client jar). Create's own kinetic blocks are immune only by accident — they all
define real `AllShapes` voxel shapes, so the same fallback returns a non-full shape.

## Suggested fix

Treat a non-occluding block as non-occluding in the fallback too:

```diff
 if (shape == null) {
-    if (canOcclude) { cullingShapesByFace = occlusionShapesByFace; return; }
-    shape = getBlock().getOcclusionShape(asState());
+    if (canOcclude) { cullingShapesByFace = occlusionShapesByFace; return; }
+    // A !canOcclude block has no occlusion shape by contract; BlockBehaviour's default would
+    // hand back state.getShape(...) == a full cube for any block without a getShape override.
+    cullingShapesByFace = EMPTY_OCCLUSION_SHAPES;
+    return;
 }
```

If deriving something from the model is preferred over giving up, the derivation should at least be
intersected with "this block does not occlude" rather than allowed to reach `FULL_BLOCK`.

## Our workaround

Per-block, in our own ports: declare the truth the block already promised with `noOcclusion()`.

```java
@Override
public VoxelShape getOcclusionShape(BlockState state) { return Shapes.empty(); }
```

`public`, not `protected` — `moreculling.classTweaker` widens `BlockBehaviour.getOcclusionShape` to
public and a JVM override may not narrow access. Applied across six blocks in one mod, then swept across five sibling ports. Zero vanilla effect.

## Prior art

Searched GitHub for MoreCulling culling-shape issues; nothing matching this fallback was found.
[Issue #364 "Issue With Block State Culling"](https://github.com/FxMorin/MoreCulling/issues/364)
looks adjacent (block-state culling regression on stairs) but is a different report; not verified as
the same code path.

issues.title: [BUG] `dontCull` is ignored when Sodium is installed
issues.body: `dontCull` doesn't work when Sodium is present. The vanilla-path mixins check `moreculling$canCull()` before culling: ```java // Block_neoforgeDrawSideMixin.java if (MoreCulling.CONFIG.useBlockStateCulling && ((MoreStateCulling) thisState).moreculling$canCull()) { ``` But `BlockOcclusionCache_sodiumMixin` doesn't — it only checks the global toggle: ```java // BlockOcclusionCache_sodiumMixin.java (v1.0.8, and same on master) if (MoreCulling.CONFIG.useBlockStateCulling) { cir.setReturnValue(CullingUtils.shouldDrawSideCulling(...)); } ``` Since Sodium builds its own chunk meshes and never calls vanilla's `shouldRenderFace`, this is the only culling path that actually runs with Sodium installed — so `dontCull` entries are silently ignored. Only disabling `useBlockStateCulling` globally works around it. **Fix:** add the same `canCull()` check used in the vanilla mixins. ### Repro 1. Install Sodium + MoreCulling. 2. Add a block to `dontCull` (e.g. `antarchy:critter_cage_block`) that would otherwise get culled. 3. Its face is still culled. Disabling `useBlockStateCulling` entirely fixes it — confirming MoreCulling is the cause, not something else. 4. Log shows no `Block with id ... doesn't exist` warning, so the block ID resolved fine. ### Environment - MoreCulling 1.0.8, NeoForge 21.1.243, MC 1.21.1, Sodium 0.8.12 With Sodium and dontCull = ["antarchy:critter_cage_block"]: Without Sodium and dontCull = ["antarchy:critter_cage_block"]:

issues.title: [1.21.1 NeoForge]
issues.body:
Hello,

I found a compatibility issue between MoreCulling 1.0.7 (NeoForge 1.21.1) and Sodium 0.8.12 for Minecraft 1.21.1.

Environment

- Minecraft: 1.21.1
- Loader: NeoForge 21.1.235
- MoreCulling: 1.0.7
- Sodium: 0.8.12+mc1.21.1

Issue

The game crashes while rendering chunks. The crash appears to be caused by MoreCulling calling a Sodium method that no longer exists.

Relevant exception:

Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError:
'net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.gui.SodiumGameOptions
net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.SodiumClientMod.options()'

at ca.fxco.moreculling.utils.CullingUtils.areLeavesOpaque(CullingUtils.java:93)

The stack trace shows the crash originates in "MoreCulling" ("CullingUtils.areLeavesOpaque") during Sodium's chunk rendering pipeline.

This looks like an API incompatibility with the current Sodium version, since "SodiumClientMod.options()" appears to have been removed or changed.

I have attached the full crash report for reference.

Thank you for your work on the mod.

issues.title: [BUG] BlockEntityType issue
issues.body:
I am developping Optimized Block Entities (OBE) which is a mod made to improve the rendering of block entities. 
It decides which model to give to which entity through BlockEntityTypes, however it seems like on neoforge 1.21.1 (and maybe others), MoreCulling causes some modded block states to be considered as "valid" by a BlockEntityType (like `BlockEntityType.SIGN.isValid( some enderscape vault block )` returns true, which shouldn't be the case). I believe this caused by MoreCUlling because it happens during the phase where it caches the blockstates and it is mentionned in the logs, I might be wrong though.
This causes issues with my mods but I believe it could do so with other mods too.

Here are the issues with the logs:

https://github.com/maDU59/OptimisedBlockEntities/issues/30
> sophisticated_emerald_upgrade:emerald_backpack are being considered as "valid" by BlockEntityType.BED which then (previously, before I added some safeguard), caused an error when trying to get the BedBlock.PART property. That error happening during the reload, it would not crash and just silently failed.

https://github.com/maDU59/OptimisedBlockEntities/issues/13
> Enderscape vaults are being considered as "valid" by BlockEntityType.SIGN which then (previously, before I added some safeguard), caused an error when trying to cast it to a SignBlock. That error happening during the reload, it would not crash and just silently failed.

1. Install NeoForge 1.21.1.

issues.title: Compatibility with modern Sodium 0.8.12 alpha backports to 1.21.1
issues.body:
Hi,
I'm a maintainer on Sodium and today we published the first alpha from our graduated backport experiment. This means that we [now have Sodium 0.8.12 on 1.21.1](https://modrinth.com/mod/sodium/versions?c=alpha&g=1.21.1). You can find more information about this [in our blog post on discord](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/1077645005042233374/1501010160326414426).

We've since noticed MoreCulling interacting with Sodium and crashing. In particular the MoreCulling options don't appear on our settings screen, and when rendering leaves, the game crashes. The gist is that since 0.8.x includes many changes to various parts of Sodium, including our new Config API, mods such as Sable or this one, will encounter breakage when users (cluelessly) update modpacks with the latest published versions.

If you'd like to coordinate more closely with us, you're invited to [our discord server.](https://caffeinemc.net/discord) I intend for this to be considered a "feature" since this software is currently in alpha and not the mainline release. A lack of compatibility is not a fault on your part, but rather I would just like to notify you of the situation. I hope this doesn't cause too much trouble!

Thanks!

issues.title: [1.21.11] Fast Item Frames conflict: front face of 3D item-frame contents is culled on even rotations when itemFrame3FaceCulling is enabled
issues.body: ### Summary I found a reproducible rendering conflict between **MoreCulling** and **Fast Item Frames**. With both mods enabled, 3D item contents inside item frames (example: a normal block item) lose their **front face** at specific rotations. Pattern: - Rotation 0°: front face missing - Rotation 45°: renders correctly - Rotation 90°: front face missing - Rotation 135°: renders correctly - (same alternating behavior continues) ### Environment - Minecraft: **1.21.11** - Loader: **Fabric 0.18.4** - MoreCulling: **moreculling-fabric-1.21.11-1.6.2** - Fast Item Frames: **FastItemFrames-v21.11.1-mc1.21.11-Fabric** - Fabric API: **0.141.3+1.21.11** ### Reproduction 1. Enable MoreCulling + Fast Item Frames. 2. Keep MoreCulling item frame options enabled: - `useCustomItemFrameRenderer = true` - `useItemFrame3FaceCulling = true` 3. Place an item frame and put a 3D block item inside. 4. Rotate the item with right-click and observe alternating visibility of the front face. ### Expected The item should render consistently at all frame rotations. ### Actual The item front face is culled at even rotations (0/90/180/270), but appears at odd steps (45/135/225/315). ### Workaround Setting `useItemFrame3FaceCulling = false` completely avoids the bug while keeping both mods active. ### Technical hypothesis (conflict area) Not proposing a fix here, only sharing where the conflict appears to happen: - MoreCulling replaces item-frame rendering path in: - `ItemFrameRenderer_cullMixin` (`moreculling$optimizedRender`) - Item rendering is redirected through: - `ExtendedItemStackRenderState.moreculling$submitItemFrameItem` - then quad filtering in `ItemStackRenderState_faceCullingMixin` - The 3-face culling branch is gated by: - `useItemFrame3FaceCulling` - `dist > itemFrame3FaceCullingRange` - `frame.rotation % 2 == 0` - transform rotation checks - Fast Item Frames builds and submits a custom/synthetic `ItemFrameRenderState` from block-entity data (instead of vanilla entity path), including forced invisibility behavior. Given this, the interaction seems to happen specifically in MoreCulling’s 3-face quad-direction filtering for item-frame items when the state comes from Fast Item Frames. The even-rotation gate (`frame.rotation % 2 == 0`) matches the exact visual pattern. ### Why I’m reporting Mainly for discoverability and reproducibility, so users searching this rendering issue can identify the source and apply the known workaround.

issues.title: Suboptimal allocation rate with the Sodium BlockOcclusionCache#shouldDrawSide mixin
issues.body: The Chunk Render Task Executor thread normally has an allocation rate of less than 10-15 MB/s (usually 3.5 MB to 7 MB, but can be as high as 15 MB/s depending on render distance and the scene) normally. With MoreCulling, this number goes up by around +20-25 MB/s (totalling 30-40 MB/s). This is goes back to normal rate after removing MoreCulling. This might be wrong since the spark results blame sodium's method shouldDrawSide and not the handler Mixin method of MoreCulling for the allocations, but I'm assuming the BlockOcclusionCache_sodiumMixin#shouldDrawSide is the trigger. Likely explanation/guess of mine is that the allocations are the CallbackInfoReturnable allocations inserted inside the sodium's shouldDrawSide just before MoreCulling's handler method by Mixin. Based on my initial code analysis: - The handler injects just before getBlockState call, there is only 2 lines of code by Sodium at that point. - setReturnValue is always called if the useBlockStateCulling setting is turned on - essentially overwriting the method after 2 lines of sodium code mentioned above. - So in useBlockStateCulling scenario, adding those 2 lines and making the method an `@Overwrite` might be feasible. The issue is the scenario where useBlockStateCulling is turned off, where the rest of the method from Sodium which is long has to be replicated. I'm not sure if the original method can somehow be called with something from mixinextras/mixinsquared/conditional-mixin or other mixin-bonus libraries or something else other than overwrite from mixin, but replicating sodium's code would hurt maintainability and so I would understand if it can't be done. Feel free to close this issue in that case. - Overwrite also has the downside that if another mod injects at Sodium's shouldDrawSide it might create incompatibilities. Why the JVM can't eliminate the CallbackInfoReturnable allocation via JIT optimizations would be another question that I'm not sure of. An extra 30-40 MB/s is nothing the JVM can't handle, it can probably handle 10x of that, but it would reduce throughput as GCs happen more frequently, and if not using ZGC, cause STW pauses that make the frametime graph have jumps (I did start using ZGC, but I'm just curious as to if this can be fixed without sacrificing maintainability and compatibility, hence why im opening this issue to see if anyone has any valuable input). It could also be entirely something else and my assumption that it's CallbackInfoReturnable might be wrong, but I can see nothing else that would allocate before calling MoreCulling's handler method (if the allocation happened inside MoreCulling, the profiiler wouldn't put the blame on sodium's shouldDrawSide). The allocation is happening before handler method is called, but after sodium's first 2 lines of the method, since that's where the handler method is injected with the INVOKE target of getBlockState and At.Shift.BEFORE. Sodium's first 2 lines just save a local variable neighborPos and call setWithOffset in a MutableBlockPos, which just sets the mutable x y z fields. So the culprit must be the code injected by Mixin subsystem that allocates CallbackInfoReturnable before calling MoreCulling's handler method with it as an argument. I'm not even sure what frequency the shouldDrawSide method runs - is it called for every side of every block that's in the scene? That might explain why a simple wrapper object like CallbackInfoReturnable could add that much allocation rate. However, from the spark profile it seems to be called a total of 3 times from the Chunk Render Task Executor thread: The last one of 1.3 MB/s is negligible, the other 2 I'd say is non-trivial cost. Adding up all, 14.2 + 7 + 1.3 = 22 MB/s extra allocation rate from the mixin, or at least that's what I assume. If we exclude using overwrite for maintainability and compatibility reasons, another option would be to rewrite the more culling's shouldDrawSide to not completely replace sodium's, but rather use `@Redirect` or `@ModifyExpressionValue` or some other solution. Like I said, feel free to close this issue if that's not feasible. The extra allocation rate is non-trivial but is not a huge issue either.

issues.title: Some CurseForge versions depend on Cloth API
issues.body:
I've found that you've marked [Cloth API](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/cloth-api) (yes, the old one) as a dependency for some versions of MoreCulling:

- https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/moreculling/files/7054054/dependencies
- https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/moreculling/files/7054040/dependencies
- https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/moreculling/files/6676650/dependencies
- https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/moreculling/files/6676642/dependencies

This means that CurseForge App will try to install it when users install or update to any of those versions, causing weird crashes. Please remove that dependency on those versions, and also ensure it is not there in [default relations](https://authors.curseforge.com/#/projects/7054054/default-relations).

issues.title: License is unclear
issues.body:
The README says

>  I'm also fine if you use this mod in your modpacks, just make sure to mention it. 
>
> However I don't allow clients or other mods to merge this mod without permission, if you would like to use this mod in your client or another mod please contact me.

This seems to contradict the GPL v3 license that's on this repo.

I assume this is actually just a case of dual licensing - that is, this permission blurb at the end of the description is an additional license you can distribute the mod under instead of the GPL v3, and a GPL v3 mod or client could very well merge this one, but if that's the case it would be nice to clarify that, potentially by making two LICENSE files (i.e. LICENSE.GPL and LICENSE.Modpacks).

Yes, I admit this is a bit nitpicky.

issues.title: Custom culling shape handler triggers NPE after ViaFabricPlus protocol version change
issues.body:
### Description
MoreCulling 1.3.0’s mixin for `AbstractBlockState.customCullingShape` runs before the model manager is fully initialized when ViaFabricPlus’s target version has been modified, causing a NullPointerException in combination with ViaFabricPlus 4.1.2.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Install Minecraft 1.21.5 + Fabric 0.16.14 + Fabric API 0.121.0 + Cloth Config API 18.0.145 + MoreCulling 1.3.0 + ViaFabricPlus 4.1.2.
2. Launch the game once—initial startup completes fine.
3. Change ViaFabricPlus’s target protocol version to `1.21 - 1.21.1`.
4. Exit the game.
5. Relaunch the game—crash occurs in `initShapeCache`.

### **Crash Details**  
**Minecraft Version**: 1.21.4  
**Mod Version**: More Culling 1.2.6  
**Fabric Loader**: 0.16.10  
**Related Mods**: Sodium (0.6.9), ViaFabricPlus (4.0.2)

    at net.minecraft.class_4970$class_4971.handler$ehc000$moreculling$customCullingShape  
    ... (full stack trace in attached log)  
```  
- Full log: [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18893900/latest.log)

### **Steps to Reproduce**  
1. Install More Culling 1.2.6 with Fabric Loader 0.16.10.  *(Feather Client)*
2. Launch Minecraft 1.21.4.  
3. Crash occurs during game initialization.  

### **Expected Behavior**  
Game initializes normally without crashes.  

### **Actual Behavior**  
Game crashes with a `NullPointerException` related to `moreculling$getCullingShape`.  

### **Additional Context**  
- Crash occurs during resource reloading/initialization phase.  
- Other installed optimization mods: Sodium, Lithium, ModernFix.  

### **Notes**  
- The crash persists after removing other mods except More Culling.
- No OptiFine or conflicting resource packs are installed.

issues.title: Add sanity check to CONFIG calls from mixins triggered early on in the loading phase
issues.body:
When mod loading fails early on, (neo)forge stops firing events and loading things to attempt to recover enough to get to the mod loading failed screen. This means that things like configs may not get initialized.

Because your mod uses a mixin to a method in Minecraft that is called before this screen appears you should add sanity checks to your config getting, as there is a chance it has not loaded yet due to (neo)forge trying to limp to an error screen. If you don't do these sanity checks then crash reports generate that blame you for the error, like #324, even though the actual cause is something that happened earlier.

issues.body: The following 4 culls are not working in latest 0.27.1. - End Gateway - BlockState Culling (the following three. Maybe not all) - Top of fence - Chorus plant - Bamboo Also, these culls don't work without Sodium in 0.26.0 or earlier. "End Gateway" and "Top of fence" in 0.23.1 to 0.26.0. issues.body:
Hi, Create: Copycats+ dev here. We have received reports of this mod being incompatible with Copycats+, so I'm trying to implement compat by disabling culling for all our copycats (we already have advanced culling implemented in the block model, so culling done by this mod is redundant). However, because all of MoreCulling's API requires our blocks to implement an interface, I don't think it is possible to optionally depend on this mod, which makes the API unusable since we cannot force all users to download this mod.

Is it possible for other mods to opt out of MoreCulling using something more compatible (e.g. tags)?

issues.title: Optimize water and lava by making them more bumpy

labels.name: suggestion
labels.description: A suggestion, enhancement, feature or request

issues.body:
I originally suggested this for Sodium (https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/issues/2472), but it ended up being rejected, so it might fit better here.

Basically, the idea is: if a block with a full bottom face exists above water or lava, then the fluid height would raise such that it would be coplanar with the underside of said block. Here's a comparison:
![2024-06-06_00 28 22](https://github.com/FxMorin/MoreCulling/assets/52297970/87b500d5-a47c-48fc-be24-ca4a5b0ac132)
![2024-06-06_00 28 23](https://github.com/FxMorin/MoreCulling/assets/52297970/42edcc0f-2e3a-42de-816b-e2a7d6781598)

Since this would end up with the face 100% obscured if the block above is opaque, we could then cull it. This would eliminate lots of unneeded geometry in the Nether and above water caves, and things would also look a lot nicer from above and within the fluid as well (refer to the linked ticket for examples).

The fluid height would still snap up to full transparent blocks such as glass, but would not cull.

issues.body:
Triggering `PistonMovingBlockEntity.<clinit>` during specific period of initialization (e.g. at `Minecraft.<init>` return) with Lithium and ModernFix dynamic resources, causes it to throw `NullPointerException`. This was the reason behind a crash when activating pistons with [NBT Autocomplete](https://github.com/mt1006/mc-nbtac-mod) installed on top of these three mods, which is now fixed in version 1.2 (it skips piston block entity initialization with this specific set of mods). Although it's fixed for NBTac and it's rather unlikely it occurs or will occur with any other mod, I report it here so you can fix if you think it's worth it.

Steps to recreate this issue:
1. MC/Loader: 1.20.4 - Fabric Loader 0.15.7
2. Mods: More Culling (0.22.1), Lithium (0.12.1), ModernFix (5.13.0), NBT Autocomplete (1.1.8, not 1.2)
3. Dependencies: Fabric API (0.96.4), Cloth Config (13.0.121)
4. Enable `mixin.perf.dynamic_resources` in `config/modernfix-mixins.properties`
5. Run game and try to activate a piston.

It should most likely crash the game. There's a little chance of it not causing crash as NBTac uses another thread so in theory main thread can be faster with initialization, but through my testing it never happened.

issues.title: [mc1.20.1] More Culling 0.20.1 compat mixin causing incompatibilities with FerriteCore and Sodium
issues.body:
Related to #204, #205, #207, #208

The recent 0.20.1 update has been causing crashes when loading into my world (I can confirm these don't occur in 0.19.0). My crashlog pointed towards FerriteCore’s [mixin](https://github.com/malte0811/FerriteCore/blob/1.20.0/Common/src/main/java/malte0811/ferritecore/mixin/dedupmultipart/MixinMultipartModel.java) into `net.minecraft.class_1095` as the issue, which I disabled. I was then able to load into my world but all grass blocks appeared as the missing texture. I found this error in my latest.log which is probably the cause (not 100% sure though) and suggests that the recent changes to the sodium multipart compat [mixin](https://github.com/FxMorin/MoreCulling/blob/master/src/main/java/ca/fxco/moreculling/mixin/compat/MultipartBakedModel_sodiumMixin.java) (which also mixes into the same class as ferritecore) are at fault.

> [20:42:35] [Chunk Render Task Executor #0/ERROR]: Mixin apply for mod moreculling failed moreculling.mixins.json:compat.MultipartBakedModel_sodiumMixin from mod moreculling -> net.minecraft.class_1095: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InvalidInjectionException Critical injection failure: @Inject annotation on onGetQuads could not find any targets matching

issues.title: Powder snow interior faces should not be culled by non-powder snow blocks

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: suggestion
labels.description: A suggestion, enhancement, feature or request

issues.body:
The same issue as https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/issues/1163.

The inner faces of powder snow blocks should only be culled by other powder snow blocks. Having the outer faces culled by full solid opaque blocks is a good thing, but having the inner faces also culled by said blocks isn't. For example, it causes the snowy grass block's top texture to become visible, which should never happen.

Vanilla (interior appearance is desirable, but the "exterior" as viewed from Spectator mode underground is not):

issues.title: Changing how blocks interact with water

labels.name: suggestion
labels.description: A suggestion, enhancement, feature or request

issues.body:
I'm not sure if this would fit better in here or in Extra, but it seems relevant enough (unwanted faces would be culled if this was implemented).

Here's two glass blocks underwater compared with two beacons underwater:
![2023-04-22_19 37 56](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/233801121-da2e979e-baff-40bd-8b22-076aa2ce10f6.png)

As you can see, the beacons have an undesirable flowing water texture coating them. Some way to get rid of this for select blocks like beacons through the mod might be a good idea.

Sodium appears to affect this since a lot more blocks (such as signs and barriers) cause the rendering type glass causes to be used instead of how vanilla acts: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/issues/991 - I'm not sure if it'd be possible to have this mod revert those changes until a proper fix is implemented over there if both are installed at the same time.

issues.title: Make glass panes/iron bars cull each other properly when stacked vertically

labels.name: suggestion
labels.description: A suggestion, enhancement, feature or request

issues.body:
Vanilla issue https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-50349 - this has been the case for glass panes since 1.7 and for iron bars since 1.8.

In vanilla, glass panes on top of other glass panes don't cull the other glass panes, and likewise for iron bars. This results in some rather obvious stripes in large sheets formed of the blocks when seen at the correct angles, especially for iron bars.
![2023-03-30_06 31 15](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228739754-75954125-a068-4114-84d0-08fdb0b8019f.png)

It's possible to manually add in cullface arguments to the models in order to have faces be culled, however a perfect solution cannot be reached through this alone. If we assign cullface only to the "post" element, we get this:
![2023-03-30_06 32 09](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228739916-21af076c-d282-4450-a81b-22da85cb4339.png)

This is obviously incomplete, so we'd want to have the parts extending off of the post also have their tops and bottoms culled. If we add cullface accordingly, they get culled, but another issue arises: they're culled regardless, with no regard for the geometry actually above them, resulting in faces disappearing that we don't want to disappear.
![2023-03-30_06 34 33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228740261-aed7da7c-1539-4b32-b7b3-0b53155867f2.png)

In the worst case, one single post can cause four adjacent panes to not render their tops if positioned atop a cross:
![2023-03-29_19 26 01](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228740363-ebfdc791-cd0c-41de-905c-40f5d3d75140.png)
![2023-03-29_19 26 02](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228740367-795313b8-f68a-4065-b20e-d2b9e801b736.png)
![2023-03-29_19 26 25](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228740373-8b839bb9-ac90-40ea-81c9-fe9fd3009eaf.png)

Continuity has a built-in resource pack which implements cullface for panes, however since it's just a resource pack it's subject to all of the same issues (https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/issues/74). A resource pack cannot fix this issue alone - there needs to be something that takes the actual shape of blocks above it into account, rather than simply their presence.

Here are two resource packs for testing - one which only adds cullface to posts, and another that adds it to the rest of the pane:
[pane-post-cull-only.zip](https://github.com/fxmorin/MoreCulling/files/11108158/pane-post-cull-only.zip)
[pane-all-cull.zip](https://github.com/fxmorin/MoreCulling/files/11108160/pane-all-cull.zip)

issues.title: Depth-Based Leaves Culling Behaves Wrongly
issues.body:
## Introduction
It has come to my attention that MoreCulling's "Depth" setting for leaves culling works really poorly. It looks quite ugly, and its behavior doesn't match up with what I think a reasonable user would expect from a mode named "Depth." Moreover, its current results are inefficient, culling much fewer faces than it should.

To demonstrate Depth mode's current flaws, I built a long slab of Dark Oak Leaves:

![2022-12-15_16 19 26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207970420-381329a9-dd75-4385-8529-61dbf5e617dc.png)

The Redstone Block pictured above is aligned with the left-hand side of the slab of leaves. All further screenshots were taken while standing on top of the Snow on top of the Redstone Block.

## Vanilla Behavior
Here is what we see when we look through the length of the slab of leaves from the front, with Vanilla's non-culled leaves:

![2022-12-15_16 21 24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207971482-7d684880-7a7b-4234-9477-7b82cafbe09c.png)

Every front face of each leaf block down the length of the slab is being rendered. This dense coverage of leaves looks really nice, but it's pretty inefficient.

## Depth Mode - Expected Behavior
Here is what I would ***expect*** to see when I look through the leaves from the front, with Depth mode set to 1:

![2022-12-15_16 37 12](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207973329-227382ba-b82d-467e-8d36-c0f4b46b9ead.png)

Only the frontmost face of the slab of leaf blocks is being rendered. This makes sense. When I set the "Depth" to "1," I would intuitively expect that the leaves would be rendered "one-deep."

Now, here is what I would ***expect*** to see when I look through the leaves with Depth mode set to 2:

![2022-12-15_16 37 41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207973940-f84fa978-109c-4007-9bf2-22db7bd4f406.png)

Now the front faces of the two closest blocks to the camera are being rendered. This makes sense. When I set the "Depth" to "2," I would intuitively expect that the leaves would be rendered "two-deep."

## Depth Mode - Actual Current Behavior
Here is what currently happens when I look through the leaves from the front, with Depth mode set to 1:

![2022-12-15_16 50 49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207975224-e8e29692-7ce1-46c8-99a4-e80bc4d42e5f.png)

Huh, that's odd. It looks like the frontmost block is being rendered, the second block was skipped, but then all further blocks following that were rendered? Why on earth would anyone want their game to render this way? This is bizarre and inefficient!

Now, here is what currently happens when I look through the leaves with Depth mode set to 2:

![2022-12-15_16 51 27](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207975933-3bcc16ac-cbe5-4398-a468-6b6bb718fff0.png)

This is even more bizarre. The frontmost block was rendered, the second _and third_ blocks were skipped, and then the blocks begin rendering again following that. What is going on???

## How did you get those "Expected Behavior" Screenshots?
I used the mod [Cull Less Leaves](https://modrinth.com/mod/cull-less-leaves).

## Why don't you just use Cull Less Leaves in conjunction with More Culling?
I can't. Not anymore. Thanks to a new update from isXander, using these two mods in conjunction is no longer possible.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207977083-01113dd8-ce02-490b-8fe8-55db94244f33.png)\
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69320464/207977392-4c7e3b8d-0d94-4fec-b6c3-6c7f74c458a9.png)

## Desired Solution
More Culling's "Depth" mode should be rewritten to behave exactly as Cull Less Leaves does, plus any further improvements you may want to add to that. In addition, the "Fast" mode should be removed, as it would be functionally equivalent to "Depth" mode set to 1.

While I could go complain to isXander that compatibility should be re-added to Cull Less Leaves, at the end of the day, I actually think isXander is right. More Culling *does* feature leaves culling. I shouldn't have to install two mods that try to do the same thing. More Culling is the one that needs fixing.

issues.title: Cull paintings

labels.name: suggestion
labels.description: A suggestion, enhancement, feature or request

issues.body:
The mod already implements culling for item frames, an entity which cannot have faces culled in vanilla. Paintings, another entity, are a prime candidate for something to do next: by design, not only their back faces, but every face that isn't their front will always be flush against a block face, making them impossible to view if there happens to be a block occluding that face. So having these faces be culled should probably be a performance boost as well.
![2022-08-18_16 42 38](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/185519005-b4e77941-6554-4e32-8155-228ccec10c04.png)
![2022-08-18_16 42 43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/185519009-e056d700-c5e6-4ace-a032-410c8487cfda.png)
![2022-08-18_16 42 51](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/185519010-cae90d56-93d5-4135-99c6-c2a8abb351ac.png)

Also, while I haven't tested this with the mod, in vanilla paintings appear to have completely redundant internal faces when larger than 1x1, so having these faces also be removed would likely be beneficial since those can never be seen at all without clipping inside of the painting.
Likewise, it'd probably be a good idea for the edges of paintings to cull the edges of other paintings, if that's even possible...

issues.title: backport for 1 17 1 in the future
issues.body:
Why 1.17.1 is still important
This is the latest version with the old generation of the world

According to my tests, this is the most stable version of minecraft of all with a bunch of sodium and other mods
Starting from 1.18 there are strange fps drops and memory leaks

If this mod was on 1.17.1 it would be amazing
Since only on 1.17.1 you can play 32 chunks and above on not the most powerful PCs, while on 1.19.1
prolags and high memory usage begin

on 1.17.1 there is not one mod that optimizes bamboo
because of this, I and others have a lot of lag in the jungle

Many just love the old world generation and good performance

issues.title: Incompatible with DashLoader
issues.body: MoreCulling makes DashLoader [(CurseForge)](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/dashloader) [(GitHub)](https://github.com/TeamQuantumFusion/DashLoader) re-cache each time on startup. issues.title: Suggestion: Feature for Culling Powder Snow Against Solid Blocks
issues.body:
I spent sometime looking through the Java edition bug tracker, and I found one culling issue left open I wanted to leave as a suggestion if you wanted to implement it.
The bug linked here seems to note that the faces of powder snow are only culled against other powder snow blocks, and not against solid blocks. I'm not very familiar with how culling works, but I thought that a fix for this might result in a slight performance increase in areas with lots of powder snow.

issues.title: Mixin incompatibility with LibMultipart

labels.name: Mod Compatibility
labels.description: This is a compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
See Juuxel/VanillaParts#29 for the crash log. The issue is basically that MoreCulling `@Overwrite`s `Block.shouldDrawSide` while LibMultipart [tries to inject into it](https://github.com/AlexIIL/LibMultiPart/blob/211acc9a18aa04f0f2de082320b22504dd55f2d0/src/main/java/alexiil/mc/lib/multipart/mixin/impl/Client_BlockMixin.java#L29):

https://github.com/fxmorin/MoreCulling/blob/8fbbec7077bde4c7198f9c238b29e09179c41c96/src/main/java/ca/fxco/moreculling/mixin/Block_drawSideMixin.java#L23-L25

This issue will be used as a list of mods that currently don't support MoreCulling so that I can go through the mods and fix the issues.

## This has now moved over to [Compatibility Testing](https://github.com/fxmorin/MoreCulling/discussions/31#discussion-4209006)

### Supported Rendering Engines
- Vanilla
- [Fabric-Api](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric/tree/1.19/fabric-renderer-indigo) (Indigo)
- [Sodium](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric) (sodium) Added in v0.1.4
- [Indium](https://github.com/comp500/Indium)

### Currently Unsupported Mods
- None

### Currently Unsupported Rendering Engines
- None

### Rendering Engines that need testing
- [FREX](https://github.com/vram-guild/frex) (pastal)
- [Canvas](https://github.com/vram-guild/canvas) (pastal + canvas)
- [VulkanMod](https://github.com/xCollateral/VulkanMod)
- [Iris](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris)
- [Blaze4D](https://github.com/KilnGraphics/Blaze4D)

### Mods that need testing
- [BlocksToParts](https://github.com/Juuxel/BlocksToParts)
- [connected-block-textures](https://github.com/TwilightFlower/connected-block-textures)

I will put putting all this info into a wiki page before the official release of the mod. *Once this is no longer an Alpha build*

---

If you want to test if the mod is working, an easy way to do this is by using a chorus plant, and testing [this bug](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-249693)
There might be an automated system in the future, although don't get your hopes up
